tools.name: ChunkHound

tools.notes: Reference only, after a launch check that did not pass: this is a recording boundary, not a judgement on the project, which is current, MIT-licensed and documented. Upstream documents `chunkhound mcp [path]` as the stdio server, but the server never answered an MCP `initialize` request inside a fresh project within a 300-second window on this host. It failed in two different ways: left to itself uvx resolved Python 3.10, whose scipy build does not load on arm64 macOS, so the process died before accepting a connection; with Python 3.12 pinned it started but then stalled for minutes on an outbound HTTPS request with idle CPU, with and without `--no-daemon` and `--no-embeddings`, so `tools/list` was never reached. `--read-only` avoids that startup path and fails fast instead, because it needs an index that a fresh project does not have. Indexing is a separate explicit step (`chunkhound index .`), the database is created inside the project at `.chunkhound/db`, and semantic search or deep research also needs an embedding or LLM provider and credentials. Nothing here configures the tool, indexes a repository, or calls one of its tools.

tools.name: roam-code

install.runtime: uv/uvx; Python 3.12 pinned for the launcher (package requires >=3.10)

tools.notes: Pins the published PyPI release 14.1.0 with its `mcp` extra, matching upstream tag v14.1.0-r1. The launcher pins `--python 3.12` because the package requires Python >=3.10 while an unpinned `uvx` resolution on the smoke host selected Python 3.9 and exited before the MCP handshake; without the pin the entry fails on any machine whose default `python3` is older than 3.10. `roam mcp` analyses the directory the server starts in and keeps an SQLite index plus lock/state sidecars in `.roam/`; upstream documents `roam init` (index plus project configuration) and `roam index` (index only), `ROAM_DB_DIR` to relocate the store, and `ROAM_NO_AUTO_INDEX=1` to refuse implicit builds. The CLI and MCP server are Apache-2.0 and need no account or API key for local analysis; upstream's paid layers (PR Replay reports and a planned Roam Cloud) are not used by this recipe, and its README states that ordinary local analysis does not upload source code, indexes, findings or telemetry. Smoke-checked on macOS: the pinned command completed MCP initialize (server roam-code 14.1.0, protocol 2025-11-25) and listed 17 tools, including roam_search_symbol, roam_deps, roam_uses, roam_dead_code, roam_coupling, roam_taint, roam_grep, roam_file_info and roam_metrics. No tool was called when the check ran, so index quality, language coverage and answer correctness are unverified.

tools.name: orm-lens
tools.description: Answer Django model questions over MCP from static parsing — relations, ER diagrams, migration risk, N+1 candidates and schema drift — with SQLAlchemy and Alembic preview support.

install.runtime: uv/uvx; Python 3.12 pinned for the launcher (the `mcp` extra requires >=3.10)

tools.notes: Pins the published PyPI release 1.16.0 (renamed from django-orm-lens; the old name still resolves to the same distribution). The base package accepts Python >=3.9 but the `mcp` extra needs >=3.10, so the launcher pins `--python 3.12` for a deterministic resolution. The server parses model and migration files statically: upstream states it needs no database, no `runserver` and no working virtualenv, and that it still reports every app and model from a cold clone with a broken environment. Django models and migrations are the main target; SQLAlchemy models, Alembic revisions and FastAPI/Flask projects are documented as preview support. tools.notes: The normative document behind the `skill` kind in this catalog: `docs/specification.mdx` defines the `SKILL.md` frontmatter (`name`, `description`, optional `license`/`allowed-tools`/`metadata`), the directory layout and the progressive-disclosure rules that the `skill` recipes here follow, and `skills-ref/` is the Python reference implementation (`skills-ref validate <dir>`, `read-properties <dir>`, `to-prompt <dir>...`; importable API in `src/`, tests alongside, PyPI release 0.1.1, Python >=3.11, Apache-2.0). Recorded as a reference next to `anthropics/skills` and `agents-cli`: it is not a tool this installer puts into a client project, it is what to check a skill against, so there is no pinned recipe. Upstream marks `skills-ref` as demonstration-only rather than production tooling, which is recorded here as a caveat; the specification itself is what makes the entry useful. Evidence read in this pass: repository metadata, README, the `docs/` and `skills-ref/` trees, `skills-ref/README.md`, `skills-ref/pyproject.toml` and the PyPI release metadata. Nothing was installed and no skill was validated with it.

tools.description: Open-source Python framework for building MCP servers and tools: decorator API over the full MCP spec (tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation), authorization hooks, and an arcade-mcp CLI for scaffolding and running servers.
tools.name: Arcade MCP
tools.notes: Third entry in the `build-mcp` lane next to `fastmcp` and the official `mcp-python-sdk`, and the most widely deployed of the three (the README attributes 7,500+ prebuilt tools across 81 hosted MCP servers to it): a decorator API covering tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, progress and logging, `requires_auth=` declarations that let the framework own OAuth and token refresh, a vendor-neutral client story, and the `arcade-mcp` CLI for scaffolding, running and deploying servers. It is reference-only for the same reason as `fastmcp`: it is a Python library (`pyproject.toml`, monorepo `libs/arcade-core`, `libs/arcade-mcp-server`, `libs/arcade-cli`, `libs/arcade-evals`, `libs/arcade-serve`, `examples/mcp_servers/`) installed as a dependency inside a server project, not an agent-side MCP server this installer can configure by launching a command, so there is no pinned recipe; `pip install arcade-mcp` resolves PyPI 1.17.6 (Python >=3.10) and the server package publishes separately as `arcade-mcp-server` 1.33.0. MIT license. Evidence read in this pass: repository metadata, README (framework highlights and install sections), the `libs/` and `examples/` trees, and the PyPI metadata for both packages. Nothing was installed and no server was started.

tools.description: Fork of Pyright that adds Pylance features, configurable checking modes, a baseline file and an `--outputjson` report, shipped with a `basedpyright-langserver` that speaks LSP.
tools.name: basedpyright
tools.notes: Recorded next to `pyright`, `ty`, `pyrefly` and `python-lsp-server` as the third Python type checker here that also ships a language server, because it exists for the parts upstream Pyright does not open-source: Pylance-style features (inlay hints, semantic highlighting, import organization), the `recommended` and `all` checking modes, a baseline file that lets an existing project adopt strict typing incrementally instead of fixing everything at once, and a CLI report in `--outputjson` for CI. Upstream describes it as a fork of Pyright with type-checking improvements and Pylance features, and publishes a documentation site for the differences. Distribution: PyPI package `basedpyright` 1.40.2 (published 2026-10-04, Python >=3.10, bundles a Node.js runtime), a Homebrew formula, and VS Code, Open VSX and Sublime Text integrations; the launch command `basedpyright-langserver --stdio` is taken from the repository's own Zed configuration (`.zed/settings.json`). It stays reference-only for the same reason as every raw language server here: LSP does not speak MCP, so an editor or an MCP-to-LSP bridge has to start it. License note: `LICENSE.txt` carries the MIT text inherited from Pyright, the PyPI classifiers say MIT, and the GitHub API reports `NOASSERTION` because of the modified header. 3,647 stars and 138 forks on 2026-11-10; nothing was installed and no language-server or editor session was started for this entry.

tools.description: Server-side memory, handoff and experience layer for coding agents, exposed through an HTTP contract with a Python client, CLI, dashboard and a curated Agent-facing MCP projection over revisioned artifacts.
tools.name: PowerContext
tools.notes: Recorded in the memory lane that already holds `hippo-memory` and `codebase-memory-mcp`, with a different shape: memory, handoff, experience and skill are server-side artifacts behind an HTTP contract, and the Python client, CLI, dashboard, in-process Core SDK and MCP endpoint are views over the same server rather than files inside one agent's home directory. Delivery is a server the user runs and binds - `uv tool install --force "powercontext[cli,server]==1.5.1"` (PyPI 1.5.1, Apache-2.0) followed by creating the Scopes and using the returned `scope_id` - so no stdio launch command can be pinned and no install type in this catalog fits. Automatic capture additionally needs the client-side integration enabled, including trusting the PowerContext hooks in Codex, where the `UserPromptSubmit` hook is what makes prompt capture and recall run; the repository documents per-host integrations under `docs/en/docs/integrations/` (Codex is the `official` host, Claude Code and others are `community`) plus agent plugins, and all of it writes agent configuration rather than one launch entry. 1,575 stars, 631 forks and a push on 2026-11-10. Nothing was installed: no server was started, no scope was created, no hook was trusted and no MCP session was started.

tools.description: Rust language server for pytest that resolves fixture definitions across `conftest.py` and third-party plugins, and answers yield navigation, fixture call hierarchy, completion, references, rename and diagnostics for test code.
tools.name: pytest-language-server
tools.notes: Recorded for a lane no other entry covers: pytest fixture semantics. It answers go-to-definition for fixtures in the same file, in `conftest.py` files and in third-party fixtures from plugins such as pytest-mock and pytest-asyncio while respecting pytest's fixture shadowing and priority rules; jumps to the `yield` that produces a generator fixture (with teardown navigation); exposes incoming and outgoing call hierarchy so the tests and fixtures around a dependency are visible; completes fixture names inside test and fixture functions with hierarchy-aware suggestions; finds references; renames; and reports diagnostics. The README documents root markers `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg` and `.git`. It stays reference-only because it is a raw LSP binary launched as `pytest-language-server`, the same boundary as `ruff`, `pyright` and `tombi`. Distribution: PyPI `pytest-language-server` 0.26.0 (published 2026-11-03, Python >=3.10, prebuilt wheels), `uv tool install` / `pip install` / `pipx`, a Homebrew tap, crates.io, GitHub release binaries and a source build. It is early-stage and single-maintainer (Rust, 124 stars, first release November 2025) and its README states it was built with AI coding agents and reviewed afterwards, so treat it as an addition to - not a replacement for - a navigation and type server. Nothing was installed and no editor or language-server session was started.

tools.description: Trail of Bits plugin marketplace of 47 Agent Skills for security and development workflows: audit context building, differential and variant analysis, Semgrep rule authoring, property-based and mutation testing, supply-chain auditing and a modern Python project skill.
tools.name: Trail of Bits Skills
tools.notes: The most complete security-workflow skill collection found in this pass, from an upstream that publishes security research and audits: 47 plugins in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, including audit-context-building, differential-review, variant-analysis, patching-bugs, post-patch-validation, semgrep-rule-creator and semgrep-rule-variant-creator, cvss-scoring, sharp-edges, insecure-defaults, supply-chain-risk-auditor, plus traces of adjacent domains this catalog does not cover (smart contracts, malware and YARA, proofs), and a development group that does serve Python and Web work (`modern-python`, `code-improver`, `review-walkthrough`, `second-opinion`, `regression-hunt`, `property-based-testing`, `mutation-testing`, `static-analysis`, `gh-cli`, `devcontainer-setup`). It does not duplicate `security-review` (one ECC skill), `open-code-review`, or the scanner references (`semgrep`, `bandit`, `osv-scanner`, `gitleaks`, `pipelock`, `skillspector`): this is the workflow layer that decides what to audit, how to reproduce a finding and how to verify a patch, and upstream keeps a public trophy case of bugs found with it. It is reference-only because upstream delivers it as a plugin marketplace (`/plugin marketplace add trailofbits/skills`) and as per-plugin skill directories whose scripts and references differ, so there is no single subtree this catalog can pin and verify; the license is a second reason not to copy text - the content is CC-BY-SA-4.0 with a share-alike term, unlike the MIT skill collections already recorded (`anthropics/skills`, `vercel-labs/agent-skills`). 8,109 stars and 692 forks on 2026-11-10, last pushed 2026-11-06. Nothing was installed, no plugin was activated and no skill was run.
